messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Canary deployment r2025.3 is triggering elevated 5xx and latency on /v1/generate. Error rate increased to ~6% in the last 5m. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/1749004321

alice: Oncall here, picking this up. Seeing 500s and timeout spikes on canary hosts. Thanks for the ping.

ben: Confirmed from SLO dashboard — canary pool p95 latency jumped to 1.2s, overall request success dropped. Canary instances: canary-1..canary-6.

carol: I rolled r2025.3 at 12:38 PST, small canary (10%). It passed unit/regressions. Pushing a script now to pull logs.

devon: Support is getting customer reports of slow generation and some timeouts; a handful of customers see 500s on bulk generation jobs. Notifying affected customers via status page draft.

bobbot: (automated) paging ben -> oncall@sre.

alice: Ben, can you get tail of model-serving logs for canary-3 and canary-5? suspecting memory growth or aten kernel fallback.

ben: grabbing logs now. Pasting error snippet: ```
E 12:45:23    inference_server.cpp:214  KVCache miss followed by OOM on aten::matmul  
stacktrace: at runtime/conv.cc:128
runtime error: failed to allocate 512MB
```

carol: That looks like the new attention kernel in r2025.3 maybe using different memory layout. I can flip the feature flag for the new kernel for canary. Recommend kill-switch for canary kernel first.

alice: Agreed. Carol — please flip the kernel flag on canary hosts only. If unsuccessful, rollback the canary. We want minimal customer impact.

carol: Running: 
```
# flip feature flag for canary-only routing
rb feature-flag set inference.new_attn_kernel false --scope=canary --env=prod
```

carol: Command returned OK. Confirming rollout of flag change to canary group.

deploy-bot: (automated) feature-flag update applied: inference.new_attn_kernel=false scope=canary by carol.

ben: Watching metrics — error rate dropping on canary-3 within 40s. p95 latency starting to fall.

devon: Customer-facing status draft posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-0912 — marked as "Degraded: Canaries only; mitigation in progress."

alice: Nice. Keep monitoring for 10m. If error rate doesn't go <1%, initiate canary rollback.

~11 minutes later~

ben: Errors down to 0.8% across canary. Latency trending back to baseline. Looks good so far.

carol: I'll prepare a rollback plan in case we need full rollback. But since kill-switch fixed it, we should hold.

dave: From runtime team — the kernel change increased memorypressure on sequences >2048 tokens. There's a safe patch queued (r2025.3.1) but needs validation.

alice: OK. Ben — keep the oncall watch for the next 30m. Carol — coordinate with runtime to get a verified patch and coordinate an incremental canary next try. Devon — reach out to the few customers who filed tickets and confirm degraded service has resolved.

devon: Will do. I pinged two customers and they confirmed improved performance. I updated the status page to "Investigating -> Mitigated" and added note about feature flag kill-switch.

carol: Logged the rollback decision point and root-cause hypothesis in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2025-0912. Adding links to perf diffs and logs.

alice: Handoff: I'm rotating out in 30m. Ben will take second-half watch and will be primary for the next 3 hours. Ben, confirm you have context.

ben: Confirmed. I'll own until 18:00 PST then escalate if any regression. I've bookmarked dashboards, logs, and the feature-flag audit.

alice: Thanks. Postmortem owner should be runtime team + deploy. Assigning to Carol and Dave. Please include timeline, mitigation steps, and why canary didn't catch memory regression earlier.

carol: Will do. We'll also add a checklist to run long-sequence perf tests in canaries before kernel flips.

deploy-bot: (automated) incident INC-2025-0912 status updated to Mitigated by alice.

alice: Final note — no broad customer-facing rollback needed. No P0 customers impacted long-term. Closing Slack thread when Ben confirms 30m steady state. :white_check_mark:

ben: 30m steady state reached, metrics stable. Closing thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
